posts.author: StarWolff
posts.body:
alright, this is simple enough to not use scripts or plugins!
Firstly, if your moving image is the same, you could use Move Picture instead of Show Picture, you just tweak the X and Y of the image to find a placement you like, you will get way smoother transitions with it, also you won't need a wait time since it can be achieved in the Move Picture as well.
example (sorry, my MV is not in English):
Now we will need to make your event as a paralel common event (in the base data, between Tilesets and System), you'll add a switch to activate it, so if any event on the map turns the swith on, this common event will run.
Inside of the paralel common event we will call the image and make it move, for different speeds we will first create a variable for your speed, ideally starting with 0, then we will use conditional branches to check each speed, you just need to do one loop and copy paste from there, changing the time of transition in each speed.
Note that the speed will only change when the image completed one loop.
it will look like this:
there's no need for a Loop, the common event itself is looping, since it's set to Paralel
In a map event, ideally the same one you used to activate your common event, we will create a Autorum page, activated by the same switch. We need it in Autorun to stop the player movement.
In a conditional branch, go to the last page on "button" and choose one, like OK (or you can use the last option "script" and type: Input.isTriggered('ok')), so when player hits OK you add 1 to the variable.
After the branch, check if the variable has passed the number limit you want, like 5, so if variable X is bigger than 5, force back to 0).
And finally for the stop animation, check if the player hit a button like before, but with Cancel instead, and if so, delete the image and turn off the swith, stopping the loop.
it will look something like this:

posts.author: StarWolff
posts.body:
Alright, let's work on that.
Yes, if you want to change speed by selecting an option just add a +1 on the speed variable when awnsering "faster", like you would do with the button press example.
Now the first thing you need to change in your current event is that you are using two Pictures for one object, your blob is one thing, so it should be one Picture, you can use Show Picture just like the move picture if you want different images, but they are all the same Picture number.
I suggest setting a move route in a new common event using Move Picture, similar to my example above. Then, to change the graphics you'll do another common event counting the time you want the picture to change, like after a Wait of 20 frames you set Show Picture 2 (not 3) to the next frame of your animation and so on.
Note that your frames should be placed on top of eachother when looking at them all, the movement will be made using Move Picture, not by moving the frames in a editor. I mean that if you have a character jumping all the images should have similar size and same placement (all ground level) and using the move function you will make the character go up, simulating a jump.
I try to avoid using plugins so I dont have many resources and tutorials to share.

posts.author: ATT_Turan
posts.body:
A few thoughts for you:
Kunalll said:
i am still learning the game engine and still experimenting a bit.
Click to expand...
If you're still this new to MV, I'd strongly recommend you not be trying to do anything with plugins at all. Make small practice games, do the tutorials built into MV and work through some other tutorial series on YouTube and such, get familiar with how the default engine works and the included eventing system.
We get a lot of questions from people who try to jump into advanced things immediately and then ask how to do stuff that's built right into the editor.
Kunalll said:
all the tutorials just mention until how to install plugins but that's it. i have no idea how to use those plugins after installing them at all. and a lot of pages online that provide the plugins also do not have any instructions on how to use those plugins at all.
Click to expand...
That should be approximately zero percent the case
All plugins have a help file that you see when you double-click it in your plugin manager. That should include a thorough description of what it does, any plugin commands or script calls you can make, and it's also the screen where you'd see an obvious list of any plugin parameters that can be configured.
I have seen very few plugins that didn't have correct documentation like that, so I don't know where you're finding "a lot of pages" of plugins that are made poorly.
Kunalll said:
so, the following gif is something i want to achieve.
Click to expand...
Just to reiterate my original point, a bit - if you're brand new, I strongly recommend you spend some time making little practice games of the sort that RPG Maker is built to make.
Yes, you absolutely can use eventing and coding to make puzzle games or Pong in it, but you're making your learning curve harder than it needs to be by saying "I'm going to get
RPG Maker
and make Pong, which is nothing like a traditional JRPG."
Personally, I wouldn't use (and don't see a strong reason to use) a picture for this at all. I would make your center block be an event with an autonomous move route going a certain number of spaces left and right.
Then when you trigger another event (the button on the right), you can simply change the movement speed of that block event.
